Requirements: Admission to the Wildlife and Fisheries Science graduate program is based on a review of the applicant’s credentials by the WFS Graduate Faculty. The credentials consist of the Graduate School application, undergraduate and graduate transcripts, a statement of professional goals, and three letters of recommendation. To be considered for admission, applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study is required. Prerequisites for admission include at least 18 credits in the biological sciences and a minimum of 15 credits in the physical sciences (chemistry, physics, or geology) and mathematics (calculus and statistics).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Wildlife and Fisheries Science

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Ph.D. or D.Ed. programs, applicants must complete a formal Penn State Graduate School application. Requirements: Applicants must submit the following: 1. A completed online application and application fee. 2. Transcript(s) of all post-secondary work. Applicants must have a nursing degree (B.S.N. or M.S.N.) from a CCNE or ACEN accredited program. 3. An interview with a member of the program faculty. 8. Verification of physical health, background checks, and liability insurance as required by clinical agencies.
